\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 7. Topic-by-Topic Final Audit Summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\fs28 \cf0 Acting-form specificity\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. The revised baseline now distinguishes monologue, scene/duologue, screen/self-tape, stage, classical/heightened, contemporary and mixed tasks. Residual limitation: comedy and physical/fight remain conditional. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Monologue handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Monologue guidance now requires speech structure, thought shifts, stakes, rhythm, address and text handling. Residual limitation: no live examples supplied. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Scene / duologue / reader handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Reader handling is now process support; performer listening and response remain reportable only where observable. Residual limitation: reader ecology remains under-detailed. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Screen/self-tape task specificity\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Direct-to-camera, off-camera-reader, monologue, ident/slate and read-in-line contexts are separated. Residual limitation: deeper Trinity screen spec was limited. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Stage acting and heightened text handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Heightened text now requires observable sense, rhythm, imagery, thought progression and speech clarity. Residual limitation: stage-versus-screen naturalism evidence remains partly indirect. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Classical versus contemporary text\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Classical/heightened and contemporary text are separated and protected from inappropriate cross-application. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Speech / voice delivery versus singing label containment\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. Text clearly blocks singing/vocal-performance language where singing is absent. Residual limitation: frontend label behaviour remains unverified. No revision loop required; display QA required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Current vocal-as-speech proxy containment\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. The architectural proxy is contained at wording and display-semantics level without backend renaming. Residual limitation: stored field remains shared. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Technical / self-tape assessability\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Assessability is separated from acting quality and production polish. Residual limitation: reliability fallback needs output testing. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Audio / speech audibility\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Poor audio is not allowed to become weak speech performance. Residual limitation: access-conditioned positive speech descriptors remain thin. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Performance versus production-value boundary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Expensive equipment, studio polish, paid editing and cosmetic presentation are blocked as merit. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 professional_presentation boundaries\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. professional_presentation is limited to assessability, brief response, safe process and observable preparation. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Reader as process support\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Paid-reader access and reader absence are explicitly blocked as scoring evidence. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 12. Final Release Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 ACTING-FINAL-D01 \'97 Approved with explicit limitations
\f1\b0 \
The revised Acting baseline is materially compliant with ACTING-SYN-F01\'96F17 and materially responsive to ACTING-AUDIT-R01\'96R16 at wording and guardrail level. It makes Acting form-specific inside the current framework, contains spoken voice / vocal-proxy risk without schema change, separates speech audibility from speech performance, codifies self-tape assessability and anti-polish boundaries, ring-fences live-room/process-only capacities, strengthens no-brief claim restraint, protects reader handling as process support, adds accessibility-safe non-deficit language, blocks methodology overreach and prevents external frameworks becoming TapeCoach weights.\
There are no critical blockers requiring a return to ACTING-REV. The remaining issues are limitations rather than revision blockers: the structural vocal/speech proxy remains partly architecture-shaped; frontend labels, comparison labels and renderer/export timestamp behaviour are unverified; live Acting outputs were not supplied; comedy and physical/fight evidence remain limited; and some access-specific operational detail remains broad.\

\f0\b ACTING-FINAL-D02 \'97 Approved for Acting Output Specificity / Non-Regression Test Mapping with explicit limitation set
\f1\b0 \
The next stage can move forward. It must explicitly carry forward tests for label containment, acting-form specificity, screen task handling, assessability versus polish, speech audibility, reader handling, live-room overclaim, accessibility-safe language, no-brief role/world restraint, generic-feedback suppression, conditional comedy/physical/fight handling and timestamp rendering.\
Live Acting output examples are still required before product release sign-off.\
\pard\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf3 \strokec3 \
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 13. Reusable Handoff Pack for ACTING-OUTPUT-SPEC\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\fs28 \cf0 ACTING-FINAL-AUDIT handoff summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Acting final audit is complete and the revised Acting baseline is approved with explicit limitations. The revised text is materially compliant with ACTING-SYN-F01\'96F17 and materially responsive to ACTING-AUDIT-R01\'96R16. It does not alter the shared TapeCoach architecture, score fields, Acting weights, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds, role-fit bounds, report schema, backend pipeline or Musical Theatre stabilised flow.\
The strongest accepted changes are: acting-form specificity, spoken voice label containment, screen/self-tape task rules, self-tape assessability and anti-polish boundaries, speech audibility versus speech performance, live-room/process-only claim boundaries, no-brief role/world guardrails, accessibility-safe Acting and speech assessment, reader-as-process support, professional_presentation boundaries, methodology-neutrality, external-framework weighting caution, generic-feedback suppression, and timestamp / next-take specificity.\
Accepted with limitation: ACTING-REV-C02, C04, C10, C13 and C15, mainly because live frontend labels, renderer/export timestamp behaviour and live Acting outputs were not supplied. These limitations do not require another ACTING-REV pass, but they must be tested during ACTING-OUTPUT-SPEC and live QA.\
Residual risks to carry forward are: structural vocal/speech proxy semantics, unverified frontend category labels, unverified comparison-page labels, unverified renderer/export timestamp behaviour, no live Acting output examples, comedy evidence thinness, physical/fight evidence being specialist-course-shaped, methodology-neutral descriptor limits, broad neurodivergence-specific operational detail and unresolved Royal Central source limitation.\
The next stage should convert the accepted baseline into output-specificity rules and adversarial tests. Highest-priority scenarios are spoken-only no-singing label containment, monologue with no brief, reader-mediated scene, direct-to-camera versus off-camera eyeline, poor lighting/framing, poor speech audibility, smartphone/home setup, polished but weak tape, paid/basic reader, response-to-direction overclaim, training-potential overclaim, access-adapted context, speech difference, generic praise, invented role/world, physical/fight overclaim and comedy overclaim.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\fs24 \cf0 You are about to create a HANDOFF DOCUMENT for a new conversation.\
\
Goal:\
Compress all critical context from this conversation into a structured, minimal, high-signal summary that can be pasted into a new chat without loss of continuity.\
\
This handoff must preserve:\
- the completed Musical Theatre branch\
- the completed Dance branch\
- the current TapeCoach baseline constraints\
- the improved rubric-development workflow\
- the lessons learned from MT and Dance\
- the next-step process for the remaining discipline branches\
\
Do not browse.\
Do not do new research.\
Do not reopen MT or Dance.\
Do not rewrite the rubrics.\
Do not create implementation plans unless listed as pending.\
Do not include conversational commentary.\
Do not ask questions.\
Output only the structured handoff.\
\
Writing rules:\
- Be concise but complete.\
- Remove repetition, fluff, and outdated ideas.\
- Prioritise confirmed decisions, stable assets, insights, constraints and next actions.\
- Use clear headings and bullets.\
- Use precise UK English.\
- Do not include raw source tables unless they are critical.\
- Do not include old citation markers as source identifiers.\
- Use stable IDs where relevant:\
  - MT-S###\
  - MT-A##\
  - DANCE-S###\
  - DANCE-SYN-F##\
  - DANCE-AUDIT-I##\
  - DANCE-AUDIT-R##\
  - DANCE-REV-C##\
  - DANCE-REV-S##\
  - DANCE-OS-R##\
  - DANCE-OS-T##\
- Treat this handoff as the single source of truth for the new conversation.\
\
Structure the output EXACTLY as follows:\
\
---\
\
## 1. Objective\
Summarise the overarching product and research goal:\
- build reliable, evidence-backed, discipline-specific rubric improvements for TapeCoach\
- preserve stable product behaviour\
- improve feedback specificity, evidence requirements, fairness and non-regression\
- use MT and Dance as completed process templates for the wider prompt programme\
\
## 2. Current State\
Summarise what exists today:\
- current TapeCoach product baseline\
- shared six-field scoring model\
- current audition types\
- current pipeline\
- MT branch status\
- Dance branch status\
- completed assets/handoffs\
- what has not yet been implemented in product/code\
\
Include the current shared score fields:\
- technical\
- audio\
- vocal\
- acting\
- brief_adherence\
- professional_presentation\
\
Include the current protected workflow:\
- Mux upload/preparation\
- brief extraction\
- Step 1 multimodal evidence pass\
- Step 2 text-only polish pass\
- deterministic post-processing\
- server-side score recomputation\
- caps/verdict logic\
- safety/material/presentation scrubs\
- final persistence\
- UI/report rendering\
\
## 3. Key Decisions Made\
List confirmed decisions only.\
\
Must include:\
- MT research, synthesis, audit, revision, final audit and output-specificity mapping are complete at rubric/baseline level.\
- Dance research, synthesis, audit, revision, final audit and output-specificity mapping are complete at rubric/baseline level.\
- Product/code implementation and live-output QA are not complete.\
- Preserve current six operational score fields.\
- Preserve current type-specific weights unless explicitly authorised.\
- Preserve server-side score recomputation.\
- Preserve two-step evidence/polish pipeline.\
- Preserve locked-field enforcement.\
- Preserve MT acting + song stabilised flow.\
- Treat MT and Dance improvements as wording/evidence/guardrail/report-behaviour improvements, not schema rewrites.\
- Do not import exam-board or competition percentages as TapeCoach weights.\
- Do not turn practitioner taste, marketability, fame, follower count, body/type/appearance or production polish into scoring criteria.\
- Treat access needs and adapted performance contexts as fairness/assessability issues, not talent deficits.\
\
## 4. Core Insights & Learnings\
Capture the strongest findings from MT, Dance and the lessons-learned stage.\
\
Must include:\
- MT is centred on acting-through-song, vocal technique in service of story, movement in service of story, and integration.\
- MT feedback must require lyric/phrase/beat-level evidence.\
- Dance cannot be treated as one generic movement standard.\
- Dance requires style-specific handling for ballet, contemporary/modern, jazz/modern theatre, tap, commercial, street/hip-hop and MT dance.\
- Dance assessability is a precondition: full-body or task-sufficient visibility, stable framing, readable space, audible music where relevant, low-edit continuity and simple capture.\
- Dance-only reports must not show singing/voice wording where singing is absent.\
- Choreography pickup, direction response, adaptability and stamina are mainly live-room/callback evidence unless directly shown.\
- Accessibility-safe assessment requires separating adaptation from attainment and blocking deficit inference.\
- Output specificity is the acceptance standard, not just improved rubric wording.\
- Rubric development now means: score-field semantics + evidence rules + claim-scope rules + display semantics + regression tests.\
\
## 5. Constraints & Non-Negotiables\
List technical, product, safety and design constraints.\
\
Must include:\
- Do not change backend logic without explicit approval.\
- Do not change database/report schema without explicit approval.\
- Do not change public report JSON without explicit approval.\
- Do not change score fields, weights, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds or role-fit bounds without explicit approval.\
- Do not weaken MT stabilised flow.\
- Do not allow Step 2 to invent or alter locked scores, timestamps, verdicts or evidence.\
- Do not persist raw Step 1 evidence publicly.\
- Do not penalise access needs, mobility aids, seated adaptation, reduced range, convalescence, body difference or resource limitations.\
- Do not diagnose vocal, physical, injury or health conditions from tape.\
- Keep feedback grounded in observable evidence.\
- Keep UK terminology.\
\
## 6. Open Problems / Gaps\
List what remains unresolved.\
\
Must include:\
- Product/code implementation not yet executed.\
- Live-output QA not yet run for revised MT or Dance.\
- Frontend label-helper behaviour remains unverified.\
- Comparison-page label behaviour remains unverified.\
- Renderer/export timestamp behaviour remains unverified.\
- Dance structural vocal-proxy risk remains partly architectural.\
- MT through-composed rule set remains unresolved.\
- Dance commercial/street/hip-hop descriptors remain less universal than ballet/contemporary/jazz/tap.\
- Tap evidence remains thinner outside formal frameworks.\
- Score stability and rendered-output tests still need live verification.\
- Next disciplines still require full research and rubric workflow.\
\
## 7. Active Workstreams\
Summarise current and upcoming workstreams.\
\
Must include:\
- Completed: Musical Theatre branch.\
- Completed: Dance branch.\
- Pending: next discipline branch.\
- Pending: prompt/process upgrade for remaining programme.\
- Pending: cross-discipline consistency review after all discipline branches complete.\
- Pending: final revised rubric set for approval.\
- Pending: implementation plan only after approval.\
- Pending: live output QA and product-level non-regression tests.\
\
## 8. Design / Product Principles\
List the principles that should guide future outputs.\
\
Must include:\
- Preserve stable product behaviour first.\
- Improve specificity inside the current structure before proposing structural change.\
- Every report should be grounded in:\
  - this performer\
  - this tape\
  - this material/task\
  - this style/subtype\
  - observable evidence\
- Separate:\
  - performance quality\
  - technical assessability\
  - access/fairness issues\
  - process/workflow issues\
  - live-room-only capacities\
- Generic praise without observable evidence is a failure mode.\
- Source-type boundaries must be preserved.\
- If a criterion is not observable, do not score it.\
- If evidence is weak or context-specific, mark it as limitation or defer.\
- Revision must remain traceable from source to final audit.\
\
## 9. Important Context to Preserve\
Include only critical context needed to avoid quality loss.\
\
Must include:\
- Current TapeCoach baseline and shared schema.\
- Current MT protected anchor.\
- Current Dance revised-baseline status.\
- MT and Dance stable ID systems.\
- The now-standard process:\
  Research \uc0\u8594  Synthesis \u8594  Gap Audit \u8594  Revision \u8594  Final Audit \u8594  Output Specificity / Non-Regression Test Mapping\
- The traceability chain:\
  Source ID \uc0\u8594  evidence finding \u8594  audit recommendation ID \u8594  revision change ID \u8594  final audit check \u8594  output-specificity test\
- Key MT source families and recommendation IDs are already completed and should not be reopened unless explicitly needed.\
- Key Dance source families and output rules are completed and should not be reopened unless explicitly needed.\
- Dance output-specificity rules:\
  - DANCE-OS-R01 to DANCE-OS-R14\
- Dance output test scenarios:\
  - DANCE-OS-T01 to DANCE-OS-T15\
\
## 10. What to Ignore Going Forward\
List outdated or rejected directions.\
\
Must include:\
- Old turn-based citation markers as source identifiers.\
- Any \'93strong enough to proceed\'94 shortcut that skips assigned sources.\
- Any attempt to treat pedagogy, practitioner opinion or competition criteria as direct universal scoring.\
- Any attempt to import exact external percentages or weights.\
- Any attempt to treat follower count, fame, marketability, body/type/appearance or social-media profile as talent evidence.\
- Any broad rewrite that breaks baseline constraints.\
- Any unsupported subtype rules.\
- Any product implementation step before final approval and implementation planning.\
\
## 11. Next Step\
State what the new conversation should focus on immediately.\
\
The next conversation should:\
- confirm the next discipline branch\
- generate the next best prompt for that branch\
- use the improved v2 process\
- start with the correct mode recommendation\
- require baseline reconciliation, field-semantics scan, source-family planning and traceability from the start\
\
If the next branch is Acting, Voice/Singing or Additional Audition Types, prepare the source-census prompt using the v2 process rather than the old draft prompt unchanged.\
\
## 12. Lessons Learned to Apply to the Next Branch\
Include the updated lessons learned from MT and Dance.\
\
Must include:\
\
### A. Required audit readiness checks\
Every audit must confirm:\
- synthesis handoff present\
- rubric slice under audit present\
- baseline / guardrail pack present\
- optional prior or later rubric versions present\
- exact rubric version under audit\
- optional versions are context only\
- audit may proceed\
- input ambiguity\
- source ID alias issues\
- evidence gaps constraining the audit\
- whether any high-priority recommendation depends on weak or unclear evidence\
\
### B. Source alias and counting rule\
If legacy and repaired IDs both appear:\
- create an audit-stage Source ID Alias Map\
- treat matching source names and URLs as one source group\
- prefer repaired global IDs\
- preserve legacy IDs in notes\
- do not double-count aliases\
- state exact / normalised / approximate source counts\
- do not make high-priority claims from unclear provenance\
\
### C. Recommendation traceability rule\
Every audit recommendation must include:\
- stable recommendation ID\
- rubric area\
- current risk\
- specific recommended change\
- observable evidence required\
- subtype/style affected where relevant\
- source basis\
- evidence strength\
- baseline impact: preserve / improve / replace / remove / suppress conditionally / defer\
- priority\
- implementation caution\
\
High-priority recommendations must rely on:\
- at least one high-confidence source, or\
- multiple converging medium-confidence sources\
- no unresolved provenance issue\
\
### D. Baseline compatibility rule\
Every audit must include a Baseline Compatibility Check:\
- baseline constraint affected\
- compatible: yes/no\
- reason\
- required handling\
- priority\
\
If incompatible with backend, schema, pipeline, database, data-flow, scoring fields or fixed weights, mark:\
- defer\
- or preserve baseline \'97 revise only if compatible\
\
### E. Evidence-to-rubric traceability matrix\
Every audit must include:\
- synthesis evidence finding\
- Source ID(s)\
- rubric area affected\
- audit implication\
- recommendation ID(s)\
- confidence\
\
### F. Do-not-change section\
Every audit must include:\
\'93Areas Not to Change Yet Because Evidence Is Insufficient\'94\
\
Use it for:\
- unresolved subtype/style areas\
- unsupported weighting claims\
- discipline details deferred to later research\
- practitioner opinion too subjective for scoring\
- pedagogy/context sources that do not support formal scoring\
- proposed changes that would break baseline constraints\
\
### G. Revision traceability addendum\
Every revision prompt must require:\
- list all audit recommendation IDs\
- classify each as implement / preserve only / suppress conditionally / remove / defer / not implemented because baseline-incompatible\
- do not implement defer items\
- do not implement weak-evidence items\
- do not implement unauthorised schema/backend/weight changes\
- for every implemented change, provide recommendation ID, rubric area, source basis, baseline compatibility and non-regression reason\
- for every non-implemented item, state why and whether it remains a research gap, baseline constraint or final-audit watch item\
\
### H. Final audit / non-regression check\
Every final audit must verify:\
- audit handoff present\
- original rubric slice present\
- revised rubric slice present\
- baseline guardrail pack present\
- exact revised version under audit\
- recommendation implementation matrix\
- non-regression check\
- overreach check\
- generic-feedback check\
- remaining issues\
- final decision\
\
Do not rewrite the rubric during final audit unless explicitly required.\
\
### I. Output-specificity and QA mapping\
Every branch must now end with output-specificity mapping:\
- output-specificity rules\
- adversarial scenario pack\
- preserved non-regression tests\
- display-layer verification checklist\
- residual limitation register\
- live-output QA requirements\
\
### J. Process v2 for next discipline\
Use this sequence:\
Research \uc0\u8594  Synthesis \u8594  Gap Audit \u8594  Revision \u8594  Final Audit \u8594  Output Specificity / Non-Regression Test Mapping\
\
Preserve this chain:\
Source ID \uc0\u8594  evidence finding \u8594  audit recommendation ID \u8594  revision change ID \u8594  final audit check \u8594  output-specificity test\
\
### K. New readiness gates before next discipline\
Before the next discipline begins, confirm:\
- baseline reality gate\
- protected anchor gate\
- field semantics gate\
- source-family gate\
- evidence-anchor gate\
- display verification gate\
- limitation spine gate\
- completion gate\
\
End the handoff after section 12.\
Do not add further sections.}{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\cocoartf2868

\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 This revision covers wording, evidence requirements, claim-scope rules, report guidance, exclusion language and discipline-specific guardrails for Acting inside the current shared TapeCoach architecture.\
The baseline text actually revised is the supplied 0B Acting rubric slice, with Acting-specific additions to the 0E guardrail logic. Because the supplied baseline does not contain detailed existing blocks for every required topic, several additions are presented as new Acting addenda rather than pretending they already existed.\
This revision does not cover implementation, code, database schema, report schema, public JSON structure, score calculation, backend field names, UI rendering, comparison-page labels, frontend helper logic or live-output QA.\

\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 In spoken-only Acting and Monologue reports, the stored vocal field may continue to operate internally as the speech-delivery slot, but user-facing language must not present that category as singing, vocal performance or song-based voice unless singing is actually present. In acting-only outputs, interpret this area as voice and speech delivery: audibility, clarity, diction, articulation, modulation, pace, pitch, volume and how speech serves the text, character or screen/stage task.\cell \row

\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Acting feedback must use the most specific form or medium supported by the brief, task or tape: monologue, scene/duologue, screen/self-tape, stage, classical/heightened text, contemporary text, or mixed acting task. If the form is unclear, state that and keep the language to observable shared acting evidence. Shared domains include text handling, intention, listening/response, thought shifts, stakes, rhythm/pacing, speech delivery, physical choices, camera or reader relationship where relevant, and suitability to any supplied brief. Do not treat all Acting tapes as one undifferentiated acting standard.\cell \row

\cf0 \'93Feedback should point to observable beats, objectives, transitions, reaction moments, stakes and clarity of thought.\'94\cell \row

\itap1\trowd \taflags0 \trgaph108\trleft-108 \trbrdrl\brdrnil \trbrdrr\brdrnil 
\clvertalc \clshdrawnil \clwWidth1612\clftsWidth3 \clmart10 \clmarl10 \clmarb10 \clmarr10 \clbrdrt\brdrnil \clbrdrl\brdrnil \clbrdrb\brdrnil \clbrdrr\brdrnil \clpadt20 \clpadl20 \clpadb20 \clpadr20 \gaph\cellx4320
\clvertalc \clshdrawnil \clwWidth13867\clftsWidth3 \clmart10 \clmarl10 \clmarb10 \clmarr10 \clbrdrt\brdrnil \clbrdrl\brdrnil \clbrdrb\brdrnil \clbrdrr\brdrnil \clpadt20 \clpadl20 \clpadb20 \clpadr20 \gaph\cellx8640
\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Proposed revised text\cell 
\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 In monologue work, evidence should be anchored in the structure of the speech: opening circumstance, shifts in thought, changes of action or address, stakes, rhythm, use of stillness or physical economy, speech clarity, and how the performer handles the text. Where the material is classical, Shakespearean, verse or heightened text, note text handling, sense, rhythm, imagery, thought progression and speech clarity only where they are observable. Where the material is contemporary, focus on text-specific choices, conversational rhythm, given circumstances where supplied, and behavioural clarity. Do not impose classical-text expectations on contemporary material or screen-naturalism expectations on stage-heightened material without source or brief support.\cell \row

\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Proposed revised text\cell 
\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Acting self-tape assessment must separate technical assessability from acting quality. Stronger performance claims require readable sight, audible speech, task-appropriate framing, usable eyeline or reader placement, and enough continuity to judge the acting choice. Plain domestic capture, smartphone recording, simple backgrounds and limited props/costume may be fully acceptable if the acting evidence is readable. Do not reward expensive equipment, studio polish, elaborate sets, paid editing or cosmetic presentation as acting merit. If assessability is materially limited, narrow the claim and lower reliability rather than using generic criticism.\cell \row

\cf0 Proposed revised text\cell 
\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Separate speech audibility from speech performance. Audio language should describe whether the speech is audible enough to judge. Speech-delivery language may address diction, articulation, pace, pitch, volume, modulation, clarity of thought, response to text and suitability to the acting task only where the tape allows it. Do not infer weak speech skill from poor recording quality alone. Do not treat accent, speech difference or communication support as a deficit unless the brief explicitly requires a task-specific accent/dialect and the evidence is observable and safe.\cell \row

\cf0 Every substantive Acting praise or criticism must include a behavioural evidence anchor. Generic phrases such as grounded, natural, believable, connected, good eyeline, strong choices, clear relationship, good pacing, emotionally truthful, strong presence, clear character, strong instincts, good voice, confident performance, professional self-tape, good energy or strong text work are not sufficient on their own. \pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Acting reports should prioritise timestamped behavioural evidence. For an assessable Acting or Monologue tape, timestamps should cover the beginning, middle and end where useful, and should include at least one high-value strength moment and one improvement moment where justified. Notes should identify the acting form, text moment, beat, thought shift, reader/camera relationship, speech choice, physical choice or assessability condition. Fix-first, strengths, improvements and next-take advice must connect to observable evidence. If assessability limits useful note density, state that limitation and lower reliability rather than padding the report with generic wording.\cell \row

\cf0 Acting reports should use these sections to show what was observable in this performer, this tape, this text, this role or character context where supplied, and this acting form or medium where identifiable.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f0\b \cf0 Current discipline logic
\f1\b0 \
Acting is supported through acting_scene and monologue inside the existing shared framework. Feedback should remain grounded in observable acting evidence: text handling, intention, listening, response, eyeline, reader or camera relationship, thought shifts, pacing/rhythm, stillness, physical choices, speech delivery, emotional clarity and suitability to supplied brief or material.\
Acting feedback must be form-specific where the task supports it. Use the most specific supported form or medium: monologue, scene/duologue, screen/self-tape, stage, classical/heightened text, contemporary text or mixed acting task. If the form is unclear, say so and keep language to shared observable Acting domains.\
Finished tapes can show text handling, speech clarity, camera relationship, visible physical choices, reader-mediated response and some acting choices. They must not be used to infer response to direction, group work, workshop behaviour, training potential, interview readiness or broader flexibility unless those capacities are directly shown or the context is explicitly admissions/live-stage.\

\f0\b Feedback specificity rules
\f1\b0 \
Feedback should point to observable beats, text moments, thought shifts, action/intention changes, reaction moments, stakes, speech choices, physical choices, reader/camera relationship and clarity of thought.\
Generic praise or criticism is not sufficient. Terms such as grounded, natural, believable, connected, good eyeline, strong choices, clear relationship, good pacing, emotionally truthful, strong presence, clear character, strong instincts, good voice, confident performance, professional self-tape, good energy and strong text work must be replaced with observable evidence, a timestamp, a text moment, a behavioural choice, a speech choice, a screen/stage task, or an assessability condition.\
If no brief or material context is supplied, do not invent role expectations, production world, given circumstances, accent requirements, casting fit or hidden objectives.\

\f0\b Monologue and text-type handling
\f1\b0 \
In monologue work, evidence should be anchored in the structure of the speech: opening circumstance, changes of thought, shifts in action or address, stakes, rhythm, stillness or physical economy, speech clarity and how the performer handles the text.\
Where the material is classical, Shakespearean, verse or heightened text, comment on text handling, sense, rhythm, imagery, thought progression and speech clarity only where observable. Where the material is contemporary, focus on text-specific choices, conversational rhythm, given circumstances where supplied and behavioural clarity.\

\f0\b Scene / duologue and reader handling
\f1\b0 \
In scene or duologue work, reader evidence is mediated tape evidence. It is valid to comment on the performer\'92s listening, response timing, eyeline, relationship target, thought shifts and use of cues where observable. Reader availability, paid-reader quality, off-camera reader performance or lack of an ideal reader must not be treated as the performer\'92s talent level.\

\f0\b Screen/self-tape task handling
\f1\b0 \
Screen/self-tape Acting evidence must follow the task. Direct-to-camera, off-camera-reader scenes, monologues, ident/slate tasks and read-in-line dialogue use different camera relationships. Do not apply one universal eyeline rule. Comment on eyeline, frame adaptation, non-verbal listening, stillness, physical economy, speech clarity, direct address and relation to camera only where the task makes those relevant and the tape shows them.\

\f0\b Voice/speech and audio
\f1\b0 \
Voice/speech should be labelled and described as speech delivery, not singing, for spoken-only Acting. Speech-delivery evidence may include audibility, clarity, diction, articulation, modulation, pace, pitch, volume, clarity of thought, response to text and suitability to task where observable.\
Separate speech audibility from speech performance. Do not infer weak speech skill from poor recording quality alone. Do not treat accent, speech difference or communication support as a deficit unless the brief explicitly requires a task-specific accent/dialect and the evidence is observable and safe.\

\f0\b Technical / self-tape assessability
\f1\b0 \
Acting self-tape assessment must separate technical assessability from acting quality. Stronger performance claims require readable sight, audible speech, task-appropriate framing, usable eyeline or reader placement, and enough continuity to judge the acting choice. Plain domestic capture, smartphone recording, simple backgrounds and limited props/costume may be fully acceptable if the acting evidence is readable.\
If assessability is materially limited, narrow the claim and lower reliability rather than substituting generic criticism.\

\f0\b Professional presentation boundary
\f1\b0 \
In Acting, professional_presentation should be limited to assessability, brief response, safe process and task preparation that is actually observable. It must not reward expensive equipment, professional readers, paid editing, elaborate sets, cosmetic polish, class-coded presentation, domestic set transformation, marketability, charm, \'93look\'94 or equipment access as acting merit.\

\f0\b Accessibility-safe assessment
\f1\b0 \
Acting assessment must separate access process, communication support and performance evidence. Access needs, visual impairment, neurodivergence, speech difference, mobility difference, interpreters, access workers, line-feeding, accessible scripts, additional preparation time, access riders/passports or adapted audition process must not be treated as acting deficits. Judge only what is shown and assessable in the task.\
Do not infer medical history, capability ceiling, professionalism, confidence or role suitability from access need, disability, speech difference, mobility difference or adaptation.\

\f0\b Methodology-neutrality
\f1\b0 \
Acting feedback should remain methodology-neutral. It may discuss observable intention, action, listening, response, thought shift, physical choice, text handling, stakes, rhythm, camera relationship or speech delivery. It must not require or privilege Stanislavski, Meisner, Method, Brecht, Laban, Lecoq, Viewpoints, Gaulier, Commedia dell\'92Arte or any other named methodology unless the task or brief explicitly asks for it.\

\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0

\f0\b \cf0 Acting addendum: live-room-only and process-only claim block
\f1\b0 \
The following should usually be marked as live-room-only, callback-only, admissions-specific or process-only unless directly shown: response to direction, redirection, training potential, workshop behaviour, group work, interview readiness, broader flexibility, access logistics, professional workload handling and reader availability.\

\f0\b Acting addendum: exclusion and anti-bias block
\f1\b0 \
Never use the following as positive or negative Acting scoring evidence unless strictly task-supported and safely observable: singing language in spoken-only acting, body type, appearance, \'93look\'94, protected characteristics, disability or access need as deficit, visual impairment as role-defining unless the brief requires it, neurodivergence as deficit, speech difference as deficit, mobility difference or adaptation as deficit, injury or medical diagnosis from tape, follower count, fame, social-media behaviour, marketability, bookability, expensive production value, studio polish, paid reader availability, reader absence, charm/charisma/presence without observable acting behaviour, class-coded polish, accent hierarchy, method jargon as universal scoring, inferred response to direction, inferred training potential outside admissions/training context, or invented role/world claims without brief support.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 14. Reusable Handoff Pack for ACTING-FINAL-AUDIT\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\fs28 \cf0 ACTING-REV handoff summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Acting revision is complete at wording and guardrail level. It does not alter the shared six-field architecture, Acting weights, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds, report schema, backend pipeline or Musical Theatre stabilised flow. The revision strengthens the current Acting baseline by making Acting form-specific inside the existing framework, while keeping all score fields intact.\
The most important change is containment of the spoken voice / vocal proxy risk. The revised baseline now states that, although the stored vocal field may continue to operate internally as the speech-delivery slot for Acting, spoken-only reports must not present that category as singing or vocal performance unless singing is actually present. Speech delivery is now framed as audibility, clarity, diction, articulation, modulation, pace, volume and response to text or task, with poor recording quality separated from weak speech performance.\
The second major gain is Acting-form specificity. The revised baseline now distinguishes monologue, scene/duologue, screen/self-tape, stage, classical/heightened text, contemporary text and mixed acting tasks. Screen/self-tape guidance now treats camera relationship and eyeline as task-specific rather than universal. Reader handling is now clearly bounded as process support, not a talent prerequisite.\
The third major gain is claim-scope control. Response to direction, redirection, group work, workshop behaviour, training potential and broader flexibility are now treated as live-room, admissions-specific or process-only evidence unless directly shown. The no-brief guardrail is also strengthened so role, world, production style, hidden objective and casting-fit claims must be grounded in supplied material or observable evidence.\
The fourth major gain is fairness. The revision adds explicit accessibility-safe Acting and speech rules: access needs, visual impairment, neurodivergence, speech difference, mobility difference, support workers, accessible scripts, extra preparation time and adaptation must not be treated as acting deficits. professional_presentation is now bounded to assessability, brief response and safe process, not production polish, paid readers, marketability, appearance or class-coded presentation.\
Residual limitations remain but do not block final audit: frontend labels are unverified, no live Acting outputs were supplied, comedy remains thin, physical/fight evidence is specialist-course-shaped, methodology-neutral descriptor language remains limited, and some access-specific operational detail remains broad.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

**Source-provenance limitations**

The main synthesis constraints are Royal Central’s blocked current page and fallback-only video position, partial exposure in Royal Welsh, Rose Bruford and NYU Tisch, limited deeper public exposure for Trinity Acting for Screen, contract-side extraction dependence for SAG-AFTRA, and course-shaped rather than universal evidence in the East 15 gap-fill sources.

**Confidence in overall coverage**

- **High** for admissions structure, monologue/classical-contemporary distinctions, self-tape assessability, speech-as-acting evidence, screen-task evidence, professional self-tape fairness, and non-deficit access process.
- **Medium** for general acting descriptors, stage-specific positive descriptors, duologue/reader interaction as a scoring anchor, and direct stage-versus-screen naturalism comparison.
- **Low** for comedy, broad anti-bias casting framework language, and fully operational neurodivergence-specific acting-assessment detail.

| Self-tape / screen acting guidance | Readability, framing, eyeline, audio, reader handling, props/costume restraint, production-value boundaries | Rich positive acting descriptors, stage-specific evidence, live-room evidence | Anchor assessability and screen/self-tape conditions; separate technical readability from acting quality | Workflow convenience or platform process as acting criteria | S032, S033, S034 |
| Professional body / union / casting-process | Fair process, reader burden, turnaround, page limits, privacy, nudity/stunt boundaries, production burden, access-process duties | Positive acting descriptors, text/character analysis | Constrain overclaiming from mediated process; stop production burden becoming talent evidence | Contract minima or professional logistics as acting skill | S035, S036 |
| Accessibility / fairness / inclusion | Non-deficit language, barrier removal, accessible materials, visual-impairment handling, confidential access discussion, incidental casting | Positive acting-performance descriptors | Add an access-safety overlay; separate access support, assessability and acting quality | Access supports or disclosed needs as scoring criteria | S038, S039, S040, S041 |
| Form-specific school/course gap-fill | Partial evidence on devising, clown/parody, physical storytelling, fight/choreography, embodied work | Universality, methodology neutrality, generic rubric anchoring | Fill thin branches cautiously where general evidence is absent | Specialist course language as universal Acting standards | S042, S043 |
| Practitioner / process context | Context on the mediated nature of self-tapes, extra labour, sides/cue cards | Descriptor precision, assessable domains | Support caution language around what process can and cannot prove | Thin practitioner advice as scoring anchor | S037 |

**Key Acting Assessment Frameworks Found**

The Acting branch now rests on seven distinct evidence families.

- **Official school/conservatoire audition structure** provides the strongest evidence that acting auditions are not one generic task. It shows repeated monologue/speech requirements, classical/contemporary distinctions, self-tape asks, and a clean boundary between initial tape evidence and later recall/workshop/interview evidence. Principal anchors: S001–S005, S009, S013–S020, S022–S027.
- **Formal acting descriptor frameworks** supply the clearest positive acting domains: vocal/speech control, physical expressivity, characterisation, interpretive choices, contextual understanding, and reflection. Principal anchors: S029 and S030.
- **Formal screen-acting task evidence** makes screen acting a related but non-identical context, especially through eyeline, frame adaptation, direct-to-camera tasking, dialogue with read-in lines, and non-verbal listening. Principal anchor: S031.
- **Self-tape assessability and anti-polish guidance** shows what a tape needs in order to be readable and fair: clear sight/sound, manageable domestic capture, limited props/costume, and no requirement for expensive polish. Principal anchors: S032 and S033, with B1 schools as parallel support.
- **Professional/union fairness and workload guidance** prevents self-tape burden being mistaken for acting ability. It adds page limits, proportional turnaround, reader burden rules, privacy, nudity/stunt boundaries and remote-audition fairness. Principal anchors: S035 and S036.
- **Accessibility and anti-deficit evidence** reframes acting assessment through barrier removal rather than performer fault. Principal anchors: S038–S041.
- **Physical / embodied / fight-performance gap-fill evidence** exists, but only through specialist, course-shaped sources, so it supports cautious extension rather than universal standards. Principal anchors: S042 and S043.

**Accessibility, Fairness and Anti-Bias Findings**

Acting synthesis now supports the following high-confidence access and fairness propositions.

- **Access is a barrier-removal issue, not an impairment-failure issue.** The strongest support comes from ScreenSkills and Graeae. This means later Acting outputs must separate performer support needs from acting quality. Source family: S038–S040.
- **Reasonable adjustments extend beyond mobility.** They can include material format, timing, sound, lighting, personal space, communication format, interpreters, support workers, access riders/passports and confidential handling of access information. Source family: S038, S039, S041.
- **Visual-impairment-specific audition handling is directly evidenced.** Editable scripts, advance text, line-feeding, clear verbal instruction, room/set orientation and descriptive direction are not extras; they are fair-process conditions. Source: S041.
- **Access supports and adaptations are process supports, not talent criteria.** This is the single most important anti-deficit boundary for later Acting audit and revision. Source family: S038–S041, supported by S035.
- **Incidental casting materially strengthens anti-bias handling.** It reduces the risk that disability or access need becomes an invented role-defining trait. Source: S038 and S041.
- **Access information must be handled confidentially.** This is an access-process obligation, not performer self-exposure. Source family: S038–S041.
- **Assessability, process adaptation, performance quality and role fit must remain separate concepts.** The sources do not support collapsing them into one judgement.

| Professional self-tape | May covertly reward resources | Proportionate framing, readable sound, simple setup, fair process compliance if known | S014, S032, S035, S036 | Define professionalism narrowly |
| Good energy | Vague intensity label | Pace control, sustained objective, calibrated physical/vocal drive | S029, S030, S043 | Must tie to medium and task |
| Strong text work | Useful but incomplete | Specific wording choices, thought turns, rhetorical clarity, context fit | S003, S013, S029, S033 | Require text-specific examples |

## Report and Design Implications

**Report-Structure Implications**

| Report area | What it should require | Observable evidence required | Source ID(s) | Confidence | Caution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Headline / casting insight | Medium, text/form specificity, strongest supported claim, reliability note where needed | Acting form, text type, visible strength, boundary on overclaim | S001-S005, S029-S033, S035, S038 | High | No role-fit invention without brief |
| Component breakdown, if applicable | Distinguish acting, speech, technical readability and reliability | Behavioural evidence per component | S029-S033 | High | Do not import exam-board weights |
| Category breakdown | Separate acting evidence from process or access context | Named criteria and scope | Cross-source synthesis | High | Avoid generic praise categories |
| Acting note | One or more behavioural anchors tied to text/medium | Beat, listening, objective, physical or camera evidence | S029-S031, S003, S013, S020 | High | No generic “good acting” |
| Voice/speech note | Spoken clarity, diction, modulation, natural voice where relevant | Audible text delivery evidence | S029-S031, S014, S027 | High | Never relabel as singing unless singing exists |
| Technical / self-tape assessability note | Readability conditions only | Framing, light, visibility, shot stability | S014, S017, S032, S033 | High | Technical note is not acting note |
| Audio / speech audibility note | Whether speech can be heard and judged fairly | Noise, levels, intelligibility | S032, S033, S041 | High | Poor audio reduces certainty first |
| Text / character note | Text understanding and supplied context use | Clear line thought, contextual fit, title/character/playwright info if present | S003, S013, S020, S029 | High | No invented context |
| Reader / eyeline / camera relationship note | Only where task makes it relevant | Off-lens target, direct-to-camera, cue response | S019, S031, S032, S035 | High | Task-dependent |
| Strengths | Specific observable evidence only | Named moments, actions, behaviours | Cross-source synthesis | High | No charisma shorthand |
| Improvements | Actionable, observable, medium-specific | What changed evidence would look/sound like | S029-S033 | High | Avoid live-room-only claims |
| Fix-first | Reliability-critical barrier first | Sound/frame/access issue or one primary acting clarity issue | S032, S033, S035, S038-S041 | High | Distinguish actability from observability |
| Timestamped notes | Only when evidence is visible in the tape | Exact observable moment | Cross-source synthesis | High | No speculative timestamps |
| Next-take plan | Concrete behavioural or assessability adjustment | One change in speech, eyeline, framing, text turn, reader setup | S031-S033, S035 | Medium-high | Do not prescribe unsupported live-room behaviours |
| Brief / professional standards | Only when a brief/process standard exists | Material adherence, context provision, simple process compliance | S035, S036, B1 admissions family | Medium-high | Do not infer absent brief |
| Role fit if brief exists | Use supplied role context only | Alignment to brief/text, not appearance | S003, S020, S035, S038, S041 | Medium | Never rely on “look” |
| Presentation / professional_presentation note | Narrowly defined process/readability indicators only | Submission clarity, simple framing, non-distracting setup if relevant | S014, S032, S035, S036 | Medium | Appearance, resources and polish excluded |
| Feedback reliability note | State when assessment certainty is reduced | Technical, audio, access or missing-context constraints | S032, S033, S035, S038-S041 | High | Critical for safe reporting |

**Scoring and Design Implications Only**

| Current baseline issue | Evidence-supported design implication | Source ID(s) | Confidence | Baseline compatibility | Backend impact likely | Later audit priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current “vocal” proxy risk for speech delivery | Later audit should distinguish spoken speech-delivery evidence from singing semantics while preserving current operational storage during synthesis | S029, S030, S031, S014, S027 | High | Yes | Unclear | High |
| Acting-only user-facing label risk | Acting outputs for spoken work should use acting/speech language rather than generic “vocal performance” wording | S029-S031, S014, S027 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Spoken voice/speech versus singing distinction | Spoken acting evidence should be framed as clarity, diction, audibility, modulation and relation to text/character | S029-S031 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Acting subtype specificity | Later design should branch evidence by monologue, scene/duologue, screen/self-tape, stage, and text-type context | S001-S005, S029-S033 | High | Yes | Unclear | High |
| Monologue versus scene handling | Solo and relational work require different evidence expectations | S029-S031, S003, S013 | High | Yes | Unclear | High |
| Screen/self-tape versus stage handling | Screen-specific camera/eyeline/frame rules should not be universalised to stage work | S031-S033, S029, S030 | High | Yes | Unclear | High |
| Text-type handling | Classical/heightened and contemporary text should remain distinct where source-supported | S003, S013, S020, S029, S033 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Technical/video assessability | Technical readability should govern feedback certainty, not act as a covert acting criterion | S014, S017, S032, S033, S035 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Audio/speech audibility | Speech audibility can be assessed separately from acting quality | S029-S033 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Performance versus production-value boundary | Production polish, equipment burden and home-set design should be excluded from acting inference | S014, S032, S035, S036 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Acting/presence/charisma genericity risk | Later design should require behavioural anchors for generic praise terms | S029-S033 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Professional_presentation boundaries | Any presentation handling should stay narrow: readability, proportionate setup, process fairness, not appearance or expense | S014, S032, S035, S036 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Accessibility-safe acting and speech assessment | Access support and adaptation should sit as a non-deficit overlay on interpretation, speech and assessability | S038-S041, S035 | High | Yes | Unclear | High |
| Tape-observable versus live-room-only criteria | Later design should mark redirection, group work, workshop behaviour and training potential as out of tape scope unless explicit evidence exists | S001, S009, S020, S024, S035 | High | Yes | No | High |
| No-brief role/production-world invention risk | Later design should require text or brief support before role-world claims are made | S003, S013, S020, S035 | High | Yes | No | High |
| Methodology-neutrality | Later design should prefer cross-source observable constructs over method jargon | S029, S030, S038-S043 | Medium-high | Yes | No | High |

**Final Reusable Acting Handoff Pack for ACTING-AUDIT**

**Acting synthesis handoff**

The Acting branch now has a usable synthesis base covering 43 source rows across admissions, formal frameworks, self-tape/screen guidance, professional/union process sources, accessibility/inclusion sources and specialist gap-fill sources. The strongest cross-source conclusion is that Acting cannot be treated as one undifferentiated standard. Official admissions sources show repeated separation between tape evidence and live-room evidence, repeated use of monologue/speech structures, and repeated classical/contemporary distinctions. Formal frameworks add the best positive descriptor language for text handling, speech, physicality, characterisation and interpretation, while Trinity’s screen framework adds task-specific evidence for eyeline, frame adaptation, direct address, read-in-line dialogue and non-verbal listening. Self-tape guidance then strengthens assessability: readable sight/sound, simple capture, limited props/costume and anti-polish boundaries. Professional and union sources prevent mediated-tape burden from being misread as talent, adding page limits, turnaround, reader burden, privacy and no-nudity/no-stunt boundaries. Accessibility sources complete the non-deficit access spine: barrier removal, accessible materials, access riders/passports, confidential access handling, incidental casting and visual-impairment-specific adjustments. The main synthesis limitations remain explicit rather than hidden. Comedy is still thin. Rich methodology-neutral positive descriptor language remains thinner than ideal. Neurodivergence-specific acting-assessment detail is broader than it is operational. Positive acting-speech descriptors under access conditions remain stronger at process level than at descriptor level. Anti-bias casting language is materially improved but still thinner than a dedicated bias framework. Physical/embodied/fight acting is now partially mapped, but largely through specialist course-shaped sources rather than universal standards.

**Compact source-led summary**

- **Admissions / conservatoire anchors**: S001 RADA BA Acting admissions (rada.ac.uk), S003 LAMDA audition process (lamda.ac.uk), S004 Guildhall drama auditions (gsmd.ac.uk), S009 RCS BA Acting (rcs.ac.uk), S013 Mountview what to prepare (mountview.org.uk), S014 ArtsEd auditions (artsed.co.uk), S017 East 15 preparing for auditions (east15.ac.uk), S019 Manchester BA Acting audition page (theatre.mmu.ac.uk), S020 Oxford three-year acting (oxforddrama.ac.uk), S023 Yale acting application requirements (drama.yale.edu), S024 Yale acting auditions (drama.yale.edu), S026 Carnegie Mellon undergraduate admission (drama.cmu.edu), S027 USC BFA Acting for Stage and Screen (dramaticarts.usc.edu).
- **Formal and screen-task anchors**: S029 LAMDA Exams Acting (lamda.ac.uk), S030 Trinity Acting (trinitycollege.com), S031 Trinity Acting for Screen (trinitycollege.com).
- **Self-tape / assessability anchors**: S032 Spotlight self-tape essentials (spotlight.com), S033 RADA self-tape guide PDF (rada.ac.uk), with S034 Spotlight performer guide as process-only context.
- **Professional / fair-process anchors**: S035 Equity self-tape & Zoom guidance (equity.org.uk), S036 SAG-AFTRA self-tape guidelines (sagaftra.org), S037 SAG-AFTRA self-tape anatomy as process-context only.
- **Accessibility / non-deficit anchors**: S038 ScreenSkills accessible audition standard (ukstandards.org.uk), S039 ScreenSkills access coordinator skills (screenskills.com), S040 Graeae access guidance (graeae.org), S041 Equity advice for visually impaired actors (equity.org.uk).
- **Gap-fill anchors**: S042 East 15 Acting and Contemporary Theatre (east15.ac.uk), S043 East 15 Acting and Fight Performance (east15.ac.uk).

**Source-type comparison summary**

Admissions anchor audition structure and live-room boundaries. Formal frameworks anchor positive acting domains and screen-task distinctions. Self-tape guidance anchors assessability, framing, audio and anti-polish boundaries. Professional/union sources anchor fairness, burden and privacy limits. Accessibility sources anchor non-deficit adjustment and anti-inference boundaries. Gap-fill sources only cautiously extend physical/embodied/fight evidence.

**Key ACTING-SYN findings**

- ACTING-SYN-F01: Acting is not one generic standard.
- ACTING-SYN-F04: Screen acting requires task-specific camera evidence.
- ACTING-SYN-F05: Self-tape readability matters more than production polish.
- ACTING-SYN-F06: Spoken voice/speech evidence is acting evidence, not singing language.
- ACTING-SYN-F09: Professional fairness and burden rules constrain what self-tapes can be used to judge.
- ACTING-SYN-F10 and F11: Accessibility-safe assessment requires barrier removal and non-deficit handling.
- ACTING-SYN-F16: Response to direction, group work and training potential are mostly live-room or admissions-only evidence.

**Acting-form / medium / text-type criteria summary**

Monologue, scene/duologue, screen/self-tape, stage, classical/heigh­tened text and contemporary text now have usable differentiated evidence. Comedy remains thin. Physical/embodied and fight-based acting are partially covered only through specialist-course sources. Spoken voice/speech delivery is well supported as acting evidence, not singing.

**Tape-observable versus live-room-only summary**

Tape can reliably show text handling, speech clarity, camera relationship, framing awareness, visible physical choices and some reader-mediated response. Tape cannot safely prove response to direction, workshop behaviour, group work, training potential or access logistics unless explicitly provided in the evidence context.

**Self-tape / video assessability summary**

Readability depends on clear sight/sound, usable framing, simple domestic capture, limited props/costume and task-appropriate camera rules. Production polish, expensive equipment, elaborate sets and paid readers must not become proxies for acting quality.

**Accessibility / fairness summary**

Access needs are process supports, not talent deficits. Reasonable adjustments, accessible materials, extra preparation time, access riders/passports, interpreters, support workers, incidental casting and visual-impairment-specific adjustments are now explicitly evidenced.

**Generic-feedback risk list**

Grounded, natural, believable, connected, strong choices, clear relationship, good pacing, emotionally truthful, strong presence, clear character, good voice and professional self-tape are all unsafe unless tied to named observable evidence.

**Exclusion / anti-bias list**

Exclude singing language for spoken-only acting, appearance, body type, “look”, marketability, fame, follower count, class-coded polish, accent hierarchy, protected characteristics, disability/access needs as deficit, production polish as acting quality, reader availability as talent evidence, method jargon as universal scoring, inferred response to direction, and invented role/world claims without brief support.

**Evidence gaps**

Comedy; richer methodology-neutral positive acting descriptors; neurodivergence-specific acting-assessment detail; positive descriptor language for speech under access conditions; fuller anti-bias casting framework language; direct stage-versus-screen naturalism comparison; broader physical/fight evidence outside specialist-school sources; and the unresolved current Royal Central admissions source.

**Audit priorities**

Later audit should prioritise subtype specificity, spoken-speech versus singing semantics, anti-generic wording, tape-versus-live-room boundaries, production-value exclusion, access-safe non-deficit handling, no-brief claim restraint, and methodology-neutrality.

**Completion Statement**

ACTING-SYN complete. Ready for ACTING-AUDIT.{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\cocoartf2868

\f0\b \cf0 Caveats
\f1\b0 \
This bridge QA can assess MT acting+song component behaviour, generic phrase leakage, timestamp density, no-brief false specificity, presentation wording and some display-surface label issues. It cannot fully assess spoken-only Acting labels, monologue-only reports, acting_scene-only reports, Acting comparison-page labels or access-adapted Acting outputs. The final Acting audit explicitly left live Acting outputs, frontend labels, comparison labels and renderer/export timestamp parity unverified.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 15. Bridge QA Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 MT acting+song output reveals output behaviour requiring correction before broader regression execution.
\f1\b0 \

\f0\b Rationale
\f1\b0 \
The supplied MT reports preserve the most important structural MT anchor: acting and song are detected and displayed, Acting and Vocal categories remain visible where both spoken acting and singing are present, and cross-component consistency appears. That is a meaningful pass for the protected MT acting+song flow.\
However, the output behaviour is not yet safe for broader regression execution or product-level sign-off. The blocking issue is MT-BRIDGE-02: it combines brief-driven report framing and an invented 240-second rejection risk with a technical signal saying \'93No brief \'97 we\'92ll apply the professional baseline rubric.\'94 That is a critical false-specificity/no-brief failure. Across all four reports, timestamp density also fails the evidence-pass target for 3\'965 minute multi-component tapes: the attached evidence-pass standard calls for 7\'968 notes, minimum 5, while the printed reports show only 2\'964 notes. Generic praise remains common, and several reports infer recall/callback/workshop potential from a finished tape, which conflicts with the Acting live-room boundary carried through final audit.\

\f0\b Critical blockers
\f1\b0 \

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 16. Reusable Handoff Pack for Next QA Stage\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 MT-ACTING-BRIDGE-QA is complete as a bridge QA, not as full Acting live-output sign-off. Four printed MT acting+song reports and three pipeline/reference snippets were reviewed. The strongest positive result is that the protected MT structure still appears: reports show Acting Scene and Song components, visible Acting and Vocal category scores where spoken acting and singing are both present, component breakdown, and cross-component consistency. This preserves the core MT acting+song anchor and confirms that the Acting-only speech-label rule has not been wrongly applied to hide Vocal in genuine MT reports.\
The strongest failures are output-specificity failures rather than baseline-design failures. All four reports underproduce timestamped evidence for a 3\'965 minute multi-component tape: the evidence-pass target is 7\'968 notes, minimum 5, but the supplied reports render only 2\'964. A critical false-specificity issue appears in Test Result 2: the report claims brief-driven mode, a 246s/240s risk and perfect brief compliance, while technical signals say no brief and professional baseline mode. Generic praise also persists across reports: \'93grounded\'94, \'93natural\'94, \'93connected\'94, \'93believable\'94, \'93emotionally connected\'94, \'93technically excellent\'94, \'93strong vocal control\'94 and similar phrases often appear without enough behavioural evidence. Several outputs infer live-room outcomes such as callback, recall or workshop potential from finished tape evidence, which remains unsafe under ACTING-OS-R08 and ACTING-REV-C05/C14.\
ACTING-OS rule applicability summary: R02, R06, R08, R09, R11, R14, R15, R17 and R18 were directly or partially testable. R01 was only proxy-testable because singing is present. R03, R10, and several Acting-only screen/monologue tests remain untested until true Acting outputs exist.\
Bridge issue register: MT-ACTING-BRIDGE-I01 timestamp underproduction; I02 false brief/time-limit contradiction; I03 generic praise leakage; I04 live-room outcome overclaim; I05 polish/professional-presentation drift; I06 side/page reference leakage; I07 legacy confidence display; I08 acting-through-song remains too implicit.\
Required retests: no-brief MT acting+song, rendered timestamp count with report object, comparison-page parity, true spoken-only acting_scene, monologue, screen direct-to-camera, off-camera-reader scene, poor-audio/poor-framing and access-adapted Acting outputs.\
Evidence basis: ACTING-SYN-F01\'96F17, ACTING-AUDIT-I01\'96I15, ACTING-AUDIT-R01\'96R16, ACTING-REV-C01\'96C16, ACTING-REV-S01\'96S15, ACTING-FINAL-D01/D02, ACTING-OS-R01\'96R19 and ACTING-OS-T01\'96T20, with the supplied MT PDFs and pipeline snippets.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Acting branch covers 
\f0\b acting_scene
\f1\b0  and 
\f0\b monologue
\f1\b0  behaviour inside TapeCoach\'92s current shared six-field production architecture. It addresses spoken acting, monologue, scene/duologue, reader-mediated scenes, screen/self-tape tasks, stage/classical/contemporary text handling, speech delivery, self-tape assessability, professional presentation boundaries, no-brief claim restraint, accessibility-safe language, methodology neutrality, physical/fight/comedy limitations and Acting-specific output specificity.\
The revised branch outputs are intended to improve:\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 10. Live Output QA / Bridge QA Status\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 True Acting-only live outputs were 
\f0\b not supplied
\f1\b0 . True Acting live-output QA has 
\f0\b not been completed
\f1\b0 .\
A Musical Theatre acting+song bridge QA was used as partial evidence for Acting-adjacent and shared-output risks. It can show whether MT acting+song component visibility and Acting/Vocal category visibility are preserved, and whether current production outputs still show generic wording, timestamp underproduction, false specificity, polish drift or acting-through-song weakness. It cannot prove Acting-only label containment, monologue-only behaviour, acting_scene-only behaviour, Acting-only comparison labels, speech-delivery category display or access-adapted Acting output behaviour.\
Current MT production examples showed:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\ls11\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Acting and Song components displayed in MT reports.\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Vocal remained visible where singing existed.\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Generic phrases such as \'93grounded\'94, \'93naturalistic\'94, \'93emotionally connected\'94, \'93excellent vocal control\'94 and \'93professional\'94 appeared in some outputs.\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Timestamp counts were sometimes too low for a 3\'965 minute multi-component tape.\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Historical false specificity appeared around a claimed time-limit breach while the technical signal also said the length was within range.\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 professional_presentation language sometimes drifted into polish/resource wording such as \'93feels polished\'94 or \'93professional\'94, requiring stronger boundaries.\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 15. Compact Branch Handoff Pack\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Acting branch is mature enough for cross-branch consolidation and does not require an ACTING-PATCH. It is complete at research, synthesis, audit, revision, final-audit and output-specificity level, but its proposed refinements are not shipped production behaviour until later implementation and rollout.\
The branch source base contains 43 source rows across official admissions / conservatoire sources, formal acting frameworks, screen/self-tape guidance, professional and union guidance, accessibility/fairness sources and specialist form-gap sources. The strongest evidence supports acting-form specificity, the distinction between tape-observable and live-room/process evidence, speech delivery as Acting evidence rather than singing, screen/self-tape task-specific camera handling, self-tape assessability over production polish, reader-as-process support, no-brief grounding, accessibility-safe non-deficit handling and behavioural evidence anchors. Comedy, physical/fight evidence, methodology-neutral positive descriptors, neurodivergence-specific operational detail and positive speech descriptors under access conditions remain limitations rather than patch blockers.\
The audit produced ACTING-AUDIT-I01\'96I15 and ACTING-AUDIT-R01\'96R16. The revision implemented or conditionally contained these through ACTING-REV-C01\'96C16 and ACTING-REV-S01\'96S15. Final audit approved the revised baseline with explicit limitations under ACTING-FINAL-D01\'96D02. Output-specificity mapping then produced ACTING-OS-R01\'96R19, ACTING-OS-T01\'96T20 and ACTING-OS-I01\'96I10.\
Implementation-readiness implications are clear: future production Acting outputs must be form-specific, evidence-led, speech-label-safe, access-safe, anti-polish, no-brief-safe, methodology-neutral and timestamp-specific while preserving the current six-field architecture, Acting weights, server-side recomputation, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds, role-fit bounds, report schema, Step 1 / Step 2 pipeline and MT acting + song anchor.\
True Acting-only live-output QA has not been completed. The MT acting+song bridge QA provided useful partial evidence about component visibility, generic praise, timestamp underproduction, false specificity and presentation/polish drift, but it is not Acting release sign-off. Acting-only reports, comparison pages, JSON/report objects and exports are still required later to verify labels, renderer/export parity, no-brief handling, access-sensitive outputs and output enforcement.\
Stable ID families used: ACTING-S001\'96S043; ACTING-B1-F01\'96F10, ACTING-B2-F01\'96F09, ACTING-B3-F01\'96F08, ACTING-B4-F01\'96F10; ACTING-SYN-F01\'96F17; ACTING-AUDIT-I01\'96I15; ACTING-AUDIT-R01\'96R16; ACTING-REV-C01\'96C16; ACTING-REV-S01\'96S15; ACTING-FINAL-D01\'96D02; ACTING-OS-R01\'96R19; ACTING-OS-T01\'96T20; ACTING-OS-I01\'96I10.\
\pard\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0

\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0
